scope: Real Chrome (Claude in Chrome) on http://127.0.0.1:5174 against the Vite dev server of branch codex/gpu-integration; stdio connector with inspect scope only. Not the published site.

checks.name: live-page-wiring-defect-found
checks.detail: On the cherry-picked branch the connector answered 'Browser GPU environment inspection unavailable': main.js attached checkGpuEnvironment only to window.analysisApi (a copy) and not to the analysis object handed to the browser session. Unit tests injected the function and missed it.

checks.name: checkGpuEnvironment-after-wiring-fix
checks.detail: With analysis.checkGpuEnvironment wired, an inspect-scoped session returned {target:'browser', declaredCapability:{operation:'checkGpuEnvironment', declarationOnly:true}, observation:{available:true, description:'intel', isFallbackAdapter:false, maxStorageBufferBindingSize:134217728}}. The observation is a real probe of this machine; the capability declaration is kept separate from it.

checks.name: arguments-refused
checks.detail: checkGpuEnvironment with an extra argument was refused ('checkGpuEnvironment takes no arguments').

checks.name: input-unchanged-and-scope
checks.detail: The live input revision was identical before and after; an edit with the inspect-only session was refused ('Browser permission scope refused'); the contract for the method is discoverable via studio_browser_contracts (scope inspect).

regressionTest: tests/browser-gpu-inspection.test.mjs 'the live page wires checkGpuEnvironment into the analysis object handed to the browser session' (a static wiring check on src/main.js, fails without the fix).
notVerified: Only one machine/adapter was observed; fallback-adapter and no-WebGPU environments are covered by unit tests, not real browsers.
Delayed-response rejection after disconnect and device release were verified by unit tests, not in Chrome.
GPU solve correctness or performance is not claimed.
